text: By default, every visual on a report page already talks to every other one, with zero setup on your part. Here's how to actually see that happening, and exactly how to change it when the default isn't what your report needs.

Select a visual, then go to Format, Edit interactions. That single switch turns on a live control panel showing exactly how that one selected visual affects everything else sitting on the page around it. Every other visual now displays small interaction icons in its own corner.

Three options for each of those other visuals. Filter narrows what the other visual shows, so non-matching data disappears entirely. Highlight dims the rest instead, keeping everything visible while emphasizing just your selection. None means no effect at all between the two. One real exception worth remembering: line charts, scatter charts, and maps can only ever be cross-filtered, never cross-highlighted — that's a limitation of those visual types themselves, not a setting you can toggle around.

And drilling stays contained to its own visual by default, with zero effect on the rest of the page. Select the drillable visual, turn on drill-down mode, then set Apply drill down filters to Entire page — and from then on, drilling up or down there updates every other visual on the page to match. Next: drill down and drill through — moving from a summary straight to the full detail sitting behind it.
